name: GPT-NeoX-20B
description:
Here is how to read the GPT-NeoX-20B config.json. The architecture class is GPTNeoXForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 6,144: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 50,432 × 6,144: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 64, so each head sees 96 dimensions (6,144 / 64). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 6144 / 64 = 96. 96 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_hidden_layers is 44: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 24,576. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 6,144-wide stream is projected up, activated with gelu_fast, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 2,048 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is.

vocab_size is 50,432. 50,432 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is false, so the input embedding matrix and the output LM head are separate learned matrices rather than a shared transpose.

torch_dtype is float16.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/EleutherAI/GPT-NeoX-20B/blob/main/config.json.
